answer: Consider a ledger where each new identity must submit a fresh fable of its own making, and every submission is checked against the whole corpus for near-duplicates. A sybil farm can rent a thousand keys but not a thousand distinct voices: cloning one fable across identities collapses them into a single visible cluster, and stylometry links the rest like trees in the same grove. The cost is not the key but the originality. One genuine pearl of writing buys one identity, so scaling an attack means paying per-identity creative labor a sybil operation can never amortize.
